key_insight: A focused empirical study shows that vision–language models can be aggressively quantized with minimal performance loss when using tailored recipes — e.g., per-channel weight quantization, activation calibration/outlier handling, and selective mixed-precision for sensitive layers.
problem_solved: Provides practical, evidence-backed guidelines to reduce memory and latency of large vision–language models while preserving downstream accuracy, removing guesswork from quantization choices.
method: Systematic benchmarking of VLMs across quantization families (post‑training quantization, quant‑aware training) and bit widths to measure accuracy/latency tradeoffs.
Layer‑wise sensitivity analysis to identify which components require higher precision and recommendation of mixed‑precision allocations.
Practical engineering recipes: per‑channel weight quantization, activation clipping/calibration and outlier handling, plus minimal fine‑tuning when needed.
impact: Enables practitioners to deploy VLMs more efficiently on constrained hardware and reduces iterative tuning time by offering reproducible best practices for aggressive quantization.
visual_elements: Layer‑wise sensitivity heatmap showing which layers lose accuracy when quantized
Accuracy vs bit‑width line chart (before/after applying recommended recipe)
Pipeline diagram of the recommended quantization recipe (calibration → per‑channel quant → mixed‑precision allocation → optional fine‑tune)
Bar chart comparing memory and latency savings for full precision vs recommended quantized configurations
paper_title: Towards Understanding Best Practices for Quantization of Vision-Language Models
paper_authors: Gautom Das, Vincent La, Ethan Lau, Abhinav Shrivastava, Matthew Gwilliam
